attacks.obvious_combination: RISK - electrochlorination cells in parallel for ballast disinfection is a known architecture (the record's own named elements — bipolar Ti/Pt-IrO2 cells, TRO generation, ballast main — are standard), but the record does not contain a specific prior disclosure that combines them with this exact replication scheme.
attacks.contradiction: KILLED - the record states "120 kW margin" as the available power and requires 70 bench-proven cell modules in parallel at 350 m3/h, while also asserting "identical per-cell current density and electrode area" to the 5 m3/h bench pilot; the implied full-scale power demand at 70x the volumetric throughput is on the order of tens to hundreds of kW beyond what the 120 kW margin can supply under a linearly-scaled chlor-alkali load, and the record's own constraint ("120 kW margin") contradicts the unrescaled power draw its own scaling rule demands.
attacks.boundary_failure: RISK - port uptake water is stated at 2-30 C and the bench kill is demonstrated only at 30 C; the record does not contain the kinetics at 2-10 C, so the low-temperature boundary cannot be confirmed violated from the record's own numbers, but neither can it be derived to hold.
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: RISK - cathodic CaCO3/Mg(OH)2 scaling in seawater is named as a failure mode, but the record provides no current-density or Langelier saturation number to compute whether the stated operating point is inside or outside the scaling regime, so the engineering infeasibility cannot be grounded in the record's own numbers.
